name: @ostomy/api
description: Backend service: authentication, data sync, FHIR-mapped storage, and RxNorm medication lookups.
//files: CI-audit follow-up to P1.S3: this whitelist briefly held "prisma" and "prisma.config.ts" alongside "dist", because `pnpm deploy` (infra/docker/api.Dockerfile's prod-deps stage) packs a workspace's own files by this field and, at the time, `migrate` ran `prisma migrate deploy` inside that SAME pruned image `api` runs from. It no longer does — `migrate` is now its own Dockerfile stage/image (`migrate-deps` -> `migrate`) — so a single shared `files` list is no longer the right mechanism: it cannot express "pack prisma/ and prisma.config.ts for the migrate image only, not for runtime," and leaving them here would silently hand the runtime image schema/migration files it no longer has any CLI to use. `files` now names only what every `pnpm deploy` invocation of this package should ever pack ("dist"); infra/docker/api.Dockerfile's `migrate` stage COPYs prisma/schema.prisma, prisma/migrations/, and prisma.config.ts directly from the `build` stage's source checkout instead, so only that stage receives them.

scripts.test: pnpm run test:unit && pnpm run test:integration

//dependencies: `@prisma/client` and `@prisma/adapter-pg` stay ordinary dependencies: the generated client imports `@prisma/client/runtime/client` directly at runtime (verified — see prisma/schema.prisma's generator-block comment; an earlier comment here claiming otherwise was wrong and has been removed), so pruning either would break `api` itself, not just the CLI. `prisma` (the CLI) and `dotenv` moved back to devDependencies below (CI-audit follow-up to P1.S3): both were briefly promoted to dependencies so `prisma migrate deploy` could run inside the same pruned, prod-only image `api` runs from, but that made `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod` — the blocking CI gate — fail on `mysql2`/`deepmerge-ts` advisories reachable only through `prisma`'s own dependency tree, which the running API never executes. `migrate` now has its own Dockerfile stage/image (infra/docker/api.Dockerfile's `migrate-deps` -> `migrate`) built WITHOUT `--prod`, so it still gets `prisma` and `dotenv` from devDependencies. Reclassifying `prisma`/`dotenv` here was NOT by itself enough to keep either the runtime image or the CI audit gate clean, though: `@prisma/client` declares `prisma` as an `optional: true` peerDependency, and pnpm auto-links it (bringing its whole tree — `mysql2`, `postgres`, `@prisma/engines`, `@prisma/dev`, `@prisma/studio-core` — along) whenever `prisma` resolves anywhere in this workspace's shared lockfile, which it must, for this very devDependency and for `migrate` to work. Both `infra/docker/api.Dockerfile`'s `prod-deps` stage and `.github/workflows/pr.yml`'s blocking audit step add `--no-optional` for exactly this reason — see each one's own comment. `--prod` reclassification here is necessary but was not, on its own, sufficient.
